title: Water Damage Mitigation Work Authorization Terms
content:
**Work authorization terms — Water Damage Mitigation**

The job must be in dispatched status when the work authorization is signed. No extraction, tear-out or drying begins until the property owner, or an agent the owner has authorized such as the property manager of a managed property, signs the work authorization; the signature is the customer's own act. Insurance-funded jobs require no deposit, because the deductible is collected on the claim file rather than on the job. Drying equipment is set only on an authorized job.

## Retired clause
The following clause is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for collecting payment before drying equipment is set, and is kept here as a record only:

> Drying equipment may be set on a self-pay job only after customer payments posted to the job total at least the tier's self-pay deposit.

## The terms in brief
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Who may sign? | The property owner, or an agent the owner has authorized, such as the property manager of a managed property. |
| Whose act is the signature? | The customer's own. |
| In what status is the authorization signed? | Dispatched. |
| What waits on the signature? | Extraction, tear-out and drying: none of them begins before it. |
| Does an insurance-funded job pay a deposit? | No; the deductible is collected on the claim file rather than on the job. |
| On what job is drying equipment set? | Only on an authorized job. |

superseded_clauses: Drying equipment may be set on a self-pay job only after customer payments posted to the job total at least the tier's self-pay deposit.
